steps.content: Tinkle... Tinkle...
Exploration has bled you dry. Stamina gone, reserves emptied, but worse than the weariness is the loss of certainty. There is no safe path anymore. Not one.
The fog thickens ahead, swallowing everything beyond a few steps. And through it, those gazes cling to you, impossible to shake. They follow no matter where you turn, as well as the chime.
I cannot waste away like this. I must find a way forward. There is no other choice.
Ding—
Just then, a soft rustling reaches you from the side. Straining to see, you make out a hunched figure moving through the mist.

The figure wears a patchwork of brightly colored clothing and walks with a limp. Yet the damp fog, which clings to everything else, seems to have no effect on them whatsoever; they maintain their slow but steady course, heading somewhere with clear intent.
They know the way.
[Add a transition] (If no additional background image is available, add a fog effect and remove the fog afterward)

After following the figure for a while, the fog begins to thin at last, and the path resolves before you. The unsettling gazes no longer press in from all sides, and even the ringing in your ears gradually slows before fading into silence.
It worked...
Yes, your choice was right. Following the figure led you out of that perilous fog. You can breathe easy, at least for now. So then, what next?

Do you look back, hoping to glimpse what that fog truly was? Do you scout ahead, searching for a sign of where to go? Or do you simply stop and take a break? After all, this ordeal has left you utterly drained, your thoughts growing hazy at the edges.
What is going on...
You make your choice, but your body refuses to obey. Instead, it continues forward with unsteady, floating steps, trailing after the white figure ahead. Onward, onward—
Panic jolts through you. You struggle, thrash against the invisible grip, but your legs keep dragging forward. One step, then another. And then...
The path grows increasingly crowded; more figures materialize beside you, appearing from nowhere. They move as one, silent and blurred, all heading the same direction.
When you glance down, you see your own hands turning to mist, just like theirs. A leaf caught in the current, and the river will not let go.
No... Something's going wrong. I have to get away from them...

You fight. You thrash against the pull, but your feet refuse to halt, dragging you forward step by helpless step. Your body turns translucent, your breath comes in ragged gasps, and your consciousness flickers at the edges.
...Stop! Stop!
The cry tears from your throat, but your body doesn't hear. It doesn't belong to you anymore. And then, something peculiar cuts through the haze—

Stone lions line the roadside as the procession shuffles past them, blind. But you see. Crimson threads wrap around each lion, thick as rope, and their loose ends trail across the ground, coming to rest at your feet.
That's it. You can't stop moving. But if you must march, then at least you can...

options: Reach for the red threads and trip yourself

steps.content: ...Ungh!
In an instant, the torrent of figures crashes over you like floodwaters, threatening to pull you under.

options: Hold tight to the red threads

steps.content: You grip the threads with everything you have and fight your way toward where they lead.

Just as your sanity begins to fray and your strength gives out, you stumble free. The tide releases you. You collapse, gasping, heart hammering against your ribs. But slowly—blessedly—your body remembers it belongs to you again.
Pant... Pant...
You look around. The ruins have opened into a clearing, and you stand at its center, surrounded. Stone lions tower around you like silent sentinels, their bodies rising as high as buildings.
Red threads bind their eyes, layer upon layer, the trailing ends hanging down like weeping wounds. Their mouths are wide open, locked in grins that hold no warmth.

You stumble back, heart lurching, and crash into something solid. A stone statue tumbles to the ground before you, scattering rubble. You stare at its face, frozen—it wears your expression. Your terror. Your wide, uncomprehending eyes.
These statues... Could they be...?!
Fear grips you. You lash out with everything you have, your shackles screaming through the air, but the stone lions don't even scar. And still, they laugh.
The shrill laughter rises and falls in waves, each one driving deeper into your consciousness, shredding the edges of your sanity.

options: I have to get out of here!

steps.content: You spin to flee, but every path is sealed. Stone lions block every exit, towering and mocking. And among them, standing perfectly still, is a figure in white.
Bright clothing. A familiar limp. The same one who led you here.
Hitting them won't work... They helped you... You must give something in return...
You accepted their help... so you have to pay the price...
His voice is hoarse and grating, scraping against your eardrums like a saw through wood. Before you can think, the words spill from your mouth.
Then what would it—
Tinkle, tinkle, tinkle, tinkle...!
Before all the words leave your mouth, chimes shatter the silence in the distance, sharp and urgent. They cut you off. But it's already too late.

The figure lifts its head. And for the first time, you truly see: Peeling paint, not bright clothes. Crumpled folds, not wrinkled skin. Crude scissor cuts, not a human shape. And hollow, pitch-black eyes, lifting to meet yours.
<color=#fb9259>—It's a paper effigy.</color>

steps.speaker: Paper Effigy
steps.content: You want to know?

steps.speaker: Paper Effigy
steps.content: You want to know? You want to know? You want to know? You want to know?
The bell rings on frantically. The paper effigy shuffles closer, muttering under its breath.
But you can't back away. Behind you, the blood-stained stone statues wait, their grins still leering down at you from every angle.

steps.speaker: Paper Effigy
steps.content: If you want to know, then... ASK FOR IT. DEMAND IT. BEG FOR IT!!
In your dreams!
